source_caption:
To cast the deeply cynical, fiercely conflicted “fixer” at the center of his highly complex legal thriller, first-time director Tony Gilroy originally offered the title role to Denzel Washington. However, Washington was deeply hesitant to trust such a heavily nuanced, sprawling script to a completely unproven director and ultimately passed on the project. After George Clooney stepped in and delivered one of the most profoundly acclaimed performances of his entire career, Washington publicly confessed that turning down the movie was one of the biggest professional regrets of his life. By anchoring his intensely tightly-wound debut with Clooney’s deeply exhausted, quiet charisma, Gilroy masterfully proves that the most brilliant cinematic casting sometimes happens exactly when your A-list first choice walks away.
⠀
Michael Clayton (2007), directed by Tony Gilroy, starring George Clooney, Tilda Swinton, Tom Wilkinson. A deeply exhausted, highly cynical “fixer” for a massively prestigious New York corporate law firm faces a profoundly dangerous moral crisis when his brilliant but heavily unstable colleague unexpectedly sabotages a multi-billion dollar chemical lawsuit to expose a deeply ruthless, wildly lethal corporate cover-up.

source_details.title: Michael Clayton
source_details.synopsis: Michael Clayton is a 2007 American legal thriller film written and directed by Tony Gilroy in his directorial debut. It stars George Clooney as lawyer Michael Clayton, who discovers a coverup of criminal wrongdoing by one of his firm's clients. Tom Wilkinson, Tilda Swinton, and Sydney Pollack appear in supporting roles. Released on October 5, 2007, the film grossed $93 million worldwide. It was praised for Gilroy's direction and screenplay, and the performances of the cast, with Swinton's performance particularly lauded.
